content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Is it possible to continue logging data from a [product_name] controller using the [product_name] Access Tool, even without Excel being open? Thanks in advance,

Welcome to the forum. You can log data directly on the [product_name] controller, which has a small internal memory (about 1,000 bytes, operating on FIFO principle), or use an mSD card to store data as a CSV file. However, the Access Tool only functions when Excel is running.

Thanks for the quick reply! Is it possible to set up hourly data logging and visualize this data in a graph? Or to configure the logging feature to automatically add new rows in Excel? I've also tried to obtain data logs via the web server or a basic panel but couldn't get it working. Regards,

Currently, data logs stored on the SD card can only be accessed via [product_name] Soft Comfort, and only the current log is available. Alternatively, you can remove the SD card from the controller and transfer the CSV files to your PC for importing into Excel. Using the logic in your project, you can track when data was logged.
Just to clarify, there's no way to keep the controller online while passively logging data directly to a PC?

As I understand it, only the Access Tool enables live logging without requiring the controller to go into STOP mode. Passive logging can only be done via the SD card, and remote access or data review is limited to the web server or Access Tool. Is that accurate?

To read out data stored on the controller or SD card, the controller should be switched to STOP mode. Real-time logging is only possible using the Access Tool, which requires Excel to be running, as it operates as an Excel add-in.
Understood. Thanks for clarifying these details.

The issue I'm facing is that only one logger is active at a time. If you're logged in with the [product_name] Access Tool, you can't continue logging if another custom page logger tries to access the controller.

Hi, There’s one more option, though limited to I/O points. Using [product_name] Soft Comfort: go to Tools > Transfer > I/O-Status. Here, you can start recording a CSV file directly onto your PC, which logs all I/O statuses (DI, DQ, M, AI, AQ, AM, NI, etc.). Later, you only need software to read CSV files for data display. This works while the controller is in RUN mode. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience limitations in logging data from a [product_name] controller to a PC unless Excel is open, due to the design of the Access Tool as an Excel add-in. These restrictions frustrate those wanting passive or remote data collection and visualization. Only one logger can operate at a time, and options for off-site access are limited to the web server or Access Tool. While using an SD card or [product_name] Soft Comfort for CSV recording provides alternatives, each comes with technical constraints.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to passively and continuously log data from a [product_name] controller onto a PC (ideally in Excel or another accessible format) without needing Excel open, and to easily view logged data in graphical form.
